transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess… it’s the tension. My shoulders and neck are clenched pretty much all day, like I’m bracing for some classroom observation that never ends. By evening my jaw hurts, and it’s gotten hard to even enjoy playing guitar.
Did this tension start after a specific stressful event?
Yeah… I guess it did. It’s been about a year and two months, since I got fired from the preschool.
Are you still dealing with the stress from losing that preschool job?

Yeah… I think so. It’s not just missing the job. My mind keeps going over whether anyone will ever hire me again, if parents think badly of me now… whether I’ve messed up retirement. Sometimes even some tiny mistake I made in a story-time activity feels like proof I shouldn’t be trusted around kids. It just keeps circling.
Besides the job loss, do you find yourself worrying a lot about many other parts of your life too?

Yeah… it spreads. It’s mostly the job, but then it turns into everything around it — whether anyone will hire me again, whether parents think I’m… not trustworthy, whether I’ve wrecked things for retirement. Even little mistakes I made with the kids, like during story-time, I’ll keep picking at them like they prove something bad about me.
Since losing the preschool job, have you been feeling down or depressed most days?
I don’t know… I wouldn’t say depressed most days. More worn out and stuck in my head, I guess.
When the worrying starts, is it hard for you to stop or control it?

Yeah… it is. I’ll try to stop it, you know, make a list or pray, go pull weeds in the garden, just do the next thing. But it sort of… moves on to the next worry, and then another. Before I know it, half the afternoon’s gone.
Do your worries mostly come back to losing the preschool job?

Mostly, yeah. It starts there… but it doesn’t stay neat. It goes from whether anyone will hire me again, to what the parents must think, to retirement, and then I’m back picking apart some little story-time mistake like it means I can’t be trusted with kids.
Are you still unemployed?

Yes. I’ve been trying, but… not very well. I’ve missed some application deadlines, and interviews haven’t gone great. I’m not really back to volunteering for story-time unless someone else plans it, so… yeah, I’m still not back in a classroom.
In the past 6 months, have you still been under the same level of stress from losing the preschool job?
Yeah… pretty much. It’s been like this since I was fired, so… about a year and two months now.
Do you get headaches from this tension?

Not really headaches so much… it’s more my neck and shoulders. They stay clenched all day, like I’m bracing for something. By evening my jaw aches too, enough that even playing guitar isn’t really enjoyable.
If the preschool firing had never happened, do you think these worries and the tension would still be happening?
I don’t really know. I mean… it’s hard to separate it out now. Maybe some of it would’ve been there, but I can’t say for sure.
Has this worrying been making it hard for you to function day to day?

Yeah… it has. I mean, I’ve missed application deadlines, and when I do get interviews I don’t come across well. I kind of stumble through them. Even volunteering for story-time, I’ve stopped doing it unless someone else is handling the planning. So… it’s been hard to get back into a classroom in any dependable way.
Do these worries feel out of proportion to what happened with losing the preschool job?

Yes… I think so. It’s gone beyond just losing the job. My mind keeps jumping from whether anyone will ever hire me again, to whether parents think badly of me now, to whether I’ve ruined retirement somehow. Even a small mistake in a story-time activity can turn into, you know… maybe I shouldn’t be trusted with children. It feels like too much.
Do you worry a lot about things that are unrelated to losing the preschool job?

Not really unrelated, no. It usually comes back to that somehow… getting hired again, what parents think of me, whether I’ve messed up retirement. Even little things, like a mistake during story-time, can turn into… maybe I shouldn’t be around children anymore.
Before you were fired from the preschool, were you already someone who worried excessively?
No… not like this. It really started after I was fired from the preschool. It’s been about a year and a couple months now.
Is the neck-and-shoulder tension itself the main problem that brought you in today?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, the worry is there, but what finally made me come in was my neck and shoulders being clenched all day. Like I’m bracing for some classroom observation that never ends. By evening my jaw aches, and I can barely enjoy playing guitar.
Is the neck-and-shoulder pain itself what you spend most of your time worrying about?

Not mostly the pain, no. It’s more… my mind keeps going around the job stuff. Whether anyone will hire me again, what parents think, if I’ve damaged my reputation. Then it jumps to retirement, or even some little mistake with a story-time activity meaning maybe I shouldn’t be trusted with kids. The tension just sort of comes with all that.
Are you still feeling upset about being fired from the preschool?
Yeah… I guess I am. I don’t really like talking about it, but it still bothers me.
Do you feel the problems caused by being fired are still continuing in your life right now?

Yeah… it is. I’ve missed some application deadlines, and when I do get interviews I don’t come across well. I’ve also stopped doing story-time volunteering unless someone else plans it. So… it’s still getting in the way of me getting back into a classroom.
Do the worrying and muscle tension mostly happen when you think about being fired from the preschool?

Mostly, yes. It starts there, with being fired… but then it spreads. I start thinking, what if I never get hired again, or parents think badly of me now. Then it goes to retirement, and even little mistakes with a story-time activity, like maybe that means I shouldn’t be trusted with children. It’s hard to stop once it starts.
